question.knowledge_point: Sketching Cartesian Products of Special Sets in the Coordinate Plane
question.problem: Which of the following is a representation of the set $S={Z}^{-}\times N$ in the Cartesian plane?
question.worked_solution:
The Cartesian product $A\times B$ consists of all ordered pairs whose first coordinate belongs to $A$ and whose second coordinate belongs to $B.$

$$
A\times B=\{(a,b)\,:\,a\in A,\,b\in B\}
$$

In this case, the set 

$$
S={Z}^{-}\times N
$$

contains every point in ${R}^{2}$ whose $x$-coordinate is a negative integer and whose $y$-coordinate is a natural number.

$$
S=\{(x,y)\,:\,x\in {Z}^{-},\,y\in N\}.
$$

To visualize $S$, consider ${S}_{-1}⊂S$ containing all points whose $x$-coordinate equals $-1$ and whose $y$-coordinate is any natural number.

$$
{S}_{-1}=\{(-1,y)\,:\,y\in N\}.
$$

We can represent ${S}_{-1}$ in the plane as follows:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14072804/assets/8e6816767cd2010fca1b8991ed9c5e0c42d3a6d6466d78025534bc8362a174b9.png)

Next, consider ${S}_{-2}⊂S$ containing all points whose $x$-coordinate equals $-2$ and whose $y$-coordinate is any natural number.

$$
{S}_{-2}=\{(-2,y)\,:\,y\in N\}.
$$

We can represent ${S}_{-2}$ in the plane as follows:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14072804/assets/4d0fe261e790520e6a8786e6f024d5b9cb7cd54c18242103a1f4b77f09653abc.png)

We can create the subsets $…,{S}_{-5},{S}_{-4},{S}_{-3}$ similarly. Our Cartesian product $S$ is the *union* of these subsets:

$$
\begin{aligned}S & =…{S}_{-4}\cup {S}_{-3}\cup {S}_{-2}\cup {S}_{-1} \\  & ={⋃}_{i\in {Z}^{-}}{S}_{i}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we can visualize ${Z}^{-}\times N$ as the set of points in the diagram below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14072804/assets/f7e54dd973126e3179e79b1ba1a26f4a7c1c541ca764b14c4ccef73b4452509e.png)
